name: Ueno
description: Ueno from open data, lit by the real sun: the park on its hill with Toshogu's gilt hall and Kan'ei-ji's pagoda, Shinobazu Pond and Bentendo below it, and Ameyoko's market under the tracks to Okachimachi.

seawall.note: The rivers' and the bay's revetments and the castle moats: granite blocks and concrete.

trees.note: Species are not mapped, and the shared trees have no cherry or ginkgo, so the mix stands in: elms for the park's zelkovas (keyaki) and its rows of Somei-yoshino cherries, plane trees for the ginkgos and the street planes, and Japanese maples by the pond and the temple grounds. A guess, not a survey.

tour.title: Ueno, from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI's 5 m laser-scanned bare earth.

tour.title: Shinobazu Pond
tour.text: Once an inlet of the bay: three ponds below the park's hill, the lotus pond's leaves brown in November, and Bentendo on its island.

tour.title: Ameyoko after dark
tour.text: The market under the Yamanote line's viaduct, from the station to Okachimachi: fish, sweets, shoes and standing bars. The signs here are typical of the street, not its real shops'.

sources.landmarks: Kan'ei-ji's pagoda (1639; 36.4 m, Taito City), Bentendo (Kan'ei-ji; 1958), Ueno Toshogu's Konjiki-den (1651) and the statue of Saigo Takamori (Takamura Koun, 1898; 3.7 m) on OpenStreetMap's footprints and positions, their proportions from photographs. Ameyoko's signs are indicative: typical trades, no real shops' signs or logos.
sources.fonts: Signs drawn with Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License: Zen Kaku Gothic New, Dela Gothic One, M PLUS Rounded 1c, Bebas Neue, Shippori Mincho

night.note: Ameyoko's signs and the Toshogu lanterns are lit landmark meshes (city.py); the streets' lamps are the country's defaults.

game.title: Ueno on Foot
game.blurb: Walk Ueno under the real sun: up the park's steps past Saigo and his dog, round Shinobazu Pond to Bentendo, up the lantern-lined approach to Toshogu's gilt hall, and down into Ameyoko's market.

npcs.name: Noriko 典子
idle: Five museums, a concert hall and a zoo on one hill. Most people only see the pandas.
The cherries here are the city's clock: when they open, half of Tokyo has a picnic under them. {time}.

npcs.name: Daichi 大地
idle: Tuna, crab, salmon roe! In December you can't move in here.
My grandfather sold sweets from a box under the tracks in 1946. Ame, sweets: that's the name. {sun_line}

npcs.name: Sota 颯太
idle: Rowing boats, pedal boats, swan boats. The swans are the ones couples fight about.
There's an old story that couples who row here together split up. Business is still good.

npcs.name: Aoi 葵
idle: Toshogu is Tokugawa Ieyasu's shrine. The gold is real leaf; we redid it in 2013.
The peony garden opens in winter: peonies under straw hats in the snow.

quests.title: Ueno
talk: Welcome to Ueno! I'm Noriko; I guide at the National Museum on weekends.
This was the gate to the north: the trains from Tohoku came in here. Down the steps is Ameyoko. Find Daichi; he shouts louder than anyone.

quests.title: Ameyoko
talk: Ameyoko: fish on one side, sweets on the other, shoes upstairs, beer under the tracks.
Go and see the gate at the station end. Then come back hungry.

steps.text: Look down Ameyoko from its gate
Meet Saigo and his dog up the steps

quests.title: Shinobazu Pond
talk: Shinobazu Pond: three ponds, one for lotus, one for boats, one for cormorants.
Walk out to Bentendo on its island. The goddess of the hall plays the biwa; musicians come to her for luck.

quests.title: The gilt hall
talk: Up the approach between the lanterns to the Konjiki-den. Gold leaf, black lacquer, 1651.
From the approach you can see the old pagoda over the zoo's fence. It's older than the hall.
